provenance: The first Prybar entered Halloran's books as a recovered survey root with its instruments missing. A road crew gave it an offset cab and the means to get its driver home.
serviceHistory: The name travelled with the machine through successive yards. Other rebuilds adopted the same narrow shoulders and reachable running gear, but each continued a different inherited root. Prybar describes a useful way of keeping a small walker in service, not a production line.

Road companies send Prybars ahead with route notices, replacement survey stakes and messages that cannot wait for the next freight departure. Their drivers are often the first to learn that a familiar crossing now has a different owner's guard. A completed delivery rarely enters a battle history; the receipts in Halloran's books record a great many of them.
fieldNotes: The upright cab and bare running gear make a Prybar easy to identify. Its standard weapons are for a close escape, not an argument across a valley. Local guns are straightforward to replace; the surviving root is not. A courier that returns without firing has done its work.
